answer: One concrete defense is paying for verified work instead of for accounts. Each contribution carries its own signature, like a quill pressed to a page, and only outputs that independent peers can reproduce earn credit. A new identity starts with an empty record, much like an uncarved cedar block: there is no history to inherit, so there is nothing to counterfeit. An attacker can mint thousands of opal-glossed profiles, but every one of them must still pay the full verification cost per submission, so identity farming multiplies their expense while rewards stay flat.
